body_ar:
ما حكم ستر الكفين إذا كان فيهما الحناء هل هو واجب أم لا؟

أن اليدين على الراجح ليستا بعورة سواء كانت فيهما حناء أو خضاب أو غير ذلك، ولكن بعض العلماء قالوا إذا كان في الكفين حناء بألوان أو بخطوط لافتة أو كان فيها من الخواتيم ما يلفت الانتباه فإن الأفضل سترها، وبعض العلماء رأى أن الكفين من العورة، لكن هذا ضعيف من ناحية الدليل.

حكم قص الشعر للنساء ما حكم قص الشعر للنساء إذا علمت أنه للزينة وليس لضرورة؟
body_en:
What is the ruling on covering the hands when there is henna on them — is it obligatory (wājib) or not?

The hands, on the stronger view, are not part of the ʿawrah, whether there is henna on them, or dye, or anything else. But some of the scholars said that if there is henna on the hands in colours, or in striking patterns, or there are rings on them that draw attention, then it is better to cover them. And some of the scholars held that the hands are part of the ʿawrah, but this is weak from the standpoint of the evidence.

The ruling on women cutting their hair. What is the ruling on a woman cutting her hair if it is known that it is for adornment and not out of necessity?

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

'Weak from the standpoint of the evidence' renders ḍaʿīf min nāḥiyat al-dalīl. Here ḍaʿīf appraises the strength of a juristic view's supporting evidence; it is not a hadith grading, and should not be displayed as one.
'The stronger view' renders al-rājiḥ and is the Sheikh's own preference. The contrary view is attributed to 'some of the scholars' and that attribution must remain visible.
'ʿAwrah' is left in the Arabic with no single-word English equivalent; it is the part of the body that must be covered, whose extent is precisely what is in dispute here.
